business_model.claim: StealthGas sells seaborne transportation of LPG. It owns and operates LPG carriers and carries the cargo for LPG producers and users.
quotes: We own a fleet of LPG carriers providing international seaborne transportation services to LPG producers and users.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (fleet table and text)
business_model.claim: The fleet was 29 LPG carriers at year-end 2025, including one JV vessel. It was 28 at April 1, 2026, mostly small, fully pressurized gas carriers, with some semi-refrigerated and fully refrigerated ships.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we had a fleet of 29 LPG carriers, including one JV vessel.

business_model.claim: Customers are charterers: LPG producers such as national, major and independent energy companies, energy traders, and industrial users of LPG. Revenue is moderately concentrated: the three largest customers made up 34.1% of 2025 revenue versus 32.3% in 2024, and two customers each exceeded 10% of revenue in both years.
quotes: For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, our three largest customers accounted for 34.1% and 32.3%, respectively, of our revenues.

business_model.claim: Vessels are employed on time or bareboat charters (a fixed daily rate for a fixed period) or in the spot market through voyage charters. None were on bareboat charter as of April 1, 2026.
quotes: Under a time charter, the charterer pays a fixed rate per day over the term of the charter

business_model.claim: Who pays voyage costs depends on the charter type. Under time charters the company bears vessel operating costs and the charterer pays voyage costs such as fuel and port charges. Under spot or voyage charters the company bears both, so spot employment raises its voyage expenses.
quotes: Under a voyage or spot charter, we are responsible for both the vessel operating expenses and the voyage expenses incurred in performing the charter.

business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by fleet size, voyage days and daily charter hire. Revenue was $173.2 million in 2025, $167.3 million in 2024 and $143.5 million in 2023.
quotes: Our voyage revenues are driven primarily by the number and size of the vessels in our fleet

business_model.claim: The average daily time charter equivalent (TCE) rate was 15,022 in 2025, 16,080 in 2024 and 12,334 in 2023. Calendar days were 10,368, 9,944 and 10,698 in 2025, 2024 and 2023, so 2025 revenue growth came alongside a lower TCE rate than 2024.

business_model.basis: stated figures; the link between spot days and voyage costs is inferred
business_model.claim: The company is exposed to the spot market. Spot days rose to 1,385 in 2025 from 747 in 2024, and voyage expenses rose to 20,433,872 from 9,594,880.
quotes: Vessels operating in the spot market generate revenues that are less predictable but may enable us to capture increased profit margins during periods of improvements in LPG charter rates, although we are then exposed to the risk of declining LPG carrier charter rates.

quotes: StealthGas said it intends to fund the purchases from its own resources, with cash and short-term investments currently exceeding $275m and its fleet free of bank debt.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 6-K (P5) and 20-F (P1, P3); the later coverage figure is from N1.

quotes: The condition of the ship at this time remains unknown.

growth_thesis.basis: The vessels, delivery window and shareholder vote are stated in the company's 6-K items. The deal value and capacity uplift come only from the press report (inferred reliability).
growth_thesis.claim: Fleet expansion by acquisition is the main stated growth driver: a $254.6m deal for four LPG carriers from Vafias-linked companies, which a press report says would raise carrying capacity by 35%.
quotes: The Special Meeting has been called by the Board of Directors of StealthGas Inc. for the stockholders to approve the Vessel Acquisition, as defined and described in the following Notice of Special Meeting of Stockholders and accompanying Proxy Statement.

growth_thesis.basis: The cash figure is stated in the company's Q3 release, carried by a press site. The funding intention is from the press report, so partly inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: For the expansion to proceed as described, the shareholder vote must pass and the company's own cash must cover the price. A press report says the company intends to fund the purchase from its own resources and has no bank debt.
quotes: All of the vessels in the fleet are unencumbered.

growth_thesis.basis: The 60% and $115 million are stated in the Q3 release (via a press site). The 49% and 17% are stated in the 20-F. The $80m comes from a second press report.
growth_thesis.claim: Contracted charter cover supports forward revenue: about 60% of 2027 fleet days are on period charters, with about $115 million in contracted revenue across all periods. For that to continue, charterers must honor the contracts and expiring charters must be renewed on acceptable terms.
quotes: About 60% of fleet days for 2027 are secured on period charters, with total fleet employment days for all periods generating about $115 million (excl. our single JV vessel) in contracted revenues.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q3 release excerpt; the adjusted-versus-reported comparison is inferred from the printed figures.
growth_thesis.claim: Reported Q3 earnings growth came from a one-off insurance gain, not from operations. Net income was $24.5 million against $13.3 million a year earlier, but adjusted net income fell to $13.0 million from $14.4 million. For earnings growth to continue, it must come from operating results or from the added vessels, since the insurance gain will not recur.
quotes: Other operating gain for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $12.4 million compared to nil for the same period last year, resulting from the insurance claim settlement relating to vessel Eco Wizard.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q3 release (via a press site) and the Q2 release.
growth_thesis.claim: Organic revenue is shrinking because the fleet is smaller. Q3 revenue was $40.2 million against $44.5 million, based on an average of 25.0 vessels against 29.0. Growth therefore depends on the fleet base being rebuilt or rates rising.
quotes: The decrease in revenue is primarily attributable to the decreased average number of vessels in our fleet.

growth_thesis.basis: The rate-support and uncertainty statements are in the 20-F. The link to forward earnings is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Earnings power rests partly on LPG charter rates staying elevated. The 20-F ties high charter rates to the Middle East war and calls the effect of the ceasefire uncertain. For rates to hold, supply disruption must persist and spot-exposed vessels must keep earning well.
quotes: The impact of this temporary cease fire, including whether it will hold or be further extended, is uncertain, including the extent to which it may affect conditions that have supported energy prices and high charter rates for vessels that initially had resulted after the outbreak of the war.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 6-K and the 20-F; the revenue effect is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: The existing fleet's earning capacity depends on vessel availability. The company reported that the Gas Husky was struck in the Black Sea on November 17, 2026 and that its condition is unknown. The Eco Wizard had earlier been out of service since July 2025.
quotes: The condition of the ship at this time remains unknown.

material_events.basis: Stated in the 6-K filed by the company.

quotes: The condition of the ship at this time remains unknown.
